correctness.rationale: The block Gaussian Schur-complement calculation reduces the Euclidean left-projection loss to independent chi-square ratios, with an exact beta transform. Gamma-density integration yields the hypergeometric moment. Dominated convergence below the moment boundary, a rescaled beta integral above, and a controlled logarithmic integral at equality prove all sharp constants. The small-N chi-square CDF proves the rare-event constant. Symbolic exact-rational and high-precision checks reproduced the formulas and asymptotics. Assumptions n>s, 0<epsilon<1, integer p, and fixed dimensions are explicit; no finite experiment is substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: Compared the mathematical implications of the range bounds of Palitta–Portaro 2024, Saibaba 2018, Gu 2014, and Diouane et al. 2022 with the new exact fixed-spectrum Gaussian chi-square/beta distribution and full moment/rare-event phase law. Existing work establishes the algorithms, inverse-Gaussian heavy tails, and general error bounds; it does not provide the exact stated two-probe logarithmic boundary or its sharp coefficients in the inspected material. Related preceding calculations for one Gaussian probe and Gaussian Nyström do not imply the multi-column compressed inverse-Gram law as stated. The full-text comparisons reduce but do not eliminate independent priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: Classical inverse-Wishart integration may yield the same exact beta loss formula elsewhere under different terminology; independent literature-priority review remains outstanding.

value.rationale: The power-pass versus probe-count tradeoff is motivated by the row-aware construction and the known need for Gaussian oversampling. A sharp logarithmic s=2 boundary gives a natural minimal sketch-size distinction overlooked by general expectation-norm bounds. The exact constants quantify when the left sketch reaches the best possible rank-s Frobenius floor and when rare large errors persist. These results diagnose algorithm behavior rather than merely recording a renamed distribution; they are limited to an instructive spiked family.
